item.title: Collision Avoidance and Collision Detection Strategies to Counteract Large-Scale FMCW Automotive Radar Interference
item.description: arXiv:2611.13214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automotive radars operating in dense traffic environments may experience significant mutual interference, potentially degrading sensing reliability for advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS). This issue motivates the development of techniques to mitigate interference among multiple radar-equipped vehicles sharing the same spectrum. This paper investigates interference mitigation strategies for uncoordinated radar networks through system-level simulation. Two approaches are considered: frame-by-frame collision avoidance (FbF-CA), which exploits idle intervals to measure the perceived interference and possibly adapt the operating frequency, and frame-by-frame collision detection (FbF-CD), which estimates interference during transmission based on observed chirp collisions. An event-driven radar network simulator is used to model realistic highway traffic and radar interactions. Results show that collision avoidance provides higher robustness when a larger bandwidth is available, while collision detection is more effective under bandwidth-limited conditions. The analysis highlights the trade-off between collision avoidance and collision detection mitigation strategies and provides design insights for scalable automotive radar deployments.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Miccoli, Vittorio Todisco, Fabrizio Cuccoli, Matteo Passeri, Vincent Martinez, Alessandro Bazzi

item.title: Network-Co-Designed Dynamic Sparsification for Dependable Distributed Robot Learning over 3GPP Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.13282v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Robot fleets performing distributed learning often face volatile uplink conditions like bandwidth variation, packet loss, and latency spikes that delay or destabilize training. We propose a network-co-designed dynamic sparsification loop that couples model-update compression to network-facing byte budgets and time constraints. We describe two realizations: (i) a standards-aligned SA6/5GC mapping that leverages CAPIF with NEF/PCF/NWDAF, enriched with AI-specific semantics; and (ii) a VASEAL-style role-reversed loop where the learning system exposes learning-state feedback and receives bounded, time-limited control intents. We implement the mechanism in an asynchronous federated reinforcement learning framework with heterogeneous simulated quadruped robots and reproducible uplink impairments via emulated network links. Results indicate that substantial communication reduction is achievable under dynamic constraints without materially degrading learning progress in the studied setting.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: In Proc., IEEE 103rd Vehicular Technology Conference (VTC2026-Spring)
item.dc:creator: G\'eza Szab\'o, Boldizs\'ar Bunda

item.title: Confidence-Aware xApp Conflict Triage in Open RAN: A Closed-Loop ns3-oran Evaluation
item.description: arXiv:2611.13516v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the Open Radio Access Network (Open RAN), independent RAN control applications (xApps) may request changes to the same radio parameter to optimize their own KPIs, causing conflicts. When conflicts are detected via key performance indicator (KPI) degradation, current conflict management systems usually resolve them immediately, without considering how long the degradation lasts or whether the network might recover naturally, wasting radio unit (RU) energy on interventions that may not have been needed. This paper presents a confidence-aware triage layer that assesses the reliability of its predictions by calibrating intervals from past prediction errors. It also decides, for each conflict, whether to tolerate, defer, or mitigate it based on the degraded KPI prediction confidence and persistence of the conflict. It is evaluated on a common conflict between two Open RAN xApps: coverage and capacity optimization (CCO) and energy saving (ES), which issue opposing requests for transmit power and affect reference signal received power (RSRP). The triage layer is validated in a closed-loop ns3-oran simulation with 5G-LENA. Results show that the method reduces unnecessary interventions by 30% and maintains RU energy efficiency relative to fixed priority while improving it by 2.6% over the no-mitigation baseline, while maintaining a statistical safety guarantee for RSRP.
item.dc:creator: Abdul Wadud, Fatemeh Golpayegani, Nima Afraz

item.title: HERO-D3QN: Inter-Cluster Routing with Energy-Aware Soft Constraints in Wireless Sensor Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.13943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inter-cluster forwarding in wireless sensor networks can concentrate energy consumption on frequently selected relays, while hard energy thresholds restrict forwarding choices as residual energy declines. We propose Hierarchical Energy-balanced Routing Optimization based on a dueling double deep Q-network (D3QN), termed HERO-D3QN. Given the cluster structure, the method combines direction- and cost-based relay screening with energy-aware soft constraints. Relays below an adaptive energy threshold remain eligible if the other selection criteria are met. An enhanced state representation captures relay energy, progress toward the sink, potential forwarding load, and hotspot risk, and a multi-objective reward guides learning. In the comparison with D3QN using the same node locations, HERO-D3QN delayed first-node death (FND) from time step 629 to 1269 and reduced peak residual energy variance by 55.5%. In the ablation study, the full method achieved the latest FND and half-node death (HND) and the largest cumulative transmitted volume (170.52 Mbit) among the tested variants. Across five seed settings in which node locations and the random processes used in training and evaluation varied jointly, the coefficients of variation of FND, HND, and transmitted volume were 8.26%, 2.75%, and 3.88%, respectively. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of HERO-D3QN in delaying early node failure and reducing peak energy dispersion.
item.dc:creator: Weihao Wang, Heng Yang, Guangbo Chen, Shanshan Li, Jiulin Guo, Ajay Kaushik, Fangwei Li, Junrui Hao, Sixue Liu

item.title: Resilient Integrated Access and Backhaul Network Planning via Graph Neural Network Curriculum Learning
item.description: arXiv:2611.14042v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrated Access and Backhaul (IAB) is a key enabler for cost-effective millimeter-wave (mmWave) densification, yet practical deployments are strongly constrained by the spatial availability of fiber-connected IAB donors. Variations in donor topologies reshape both the initial coverage footprint and the feasible multi-hop backhaul expansion patterns, causing planning policies trained on a single topology to generalize poorly. This paper studies cross-topology generalization for resilience-aware IAB deployment under coverage and transport feasibility requirements. We formulate IAB deployment as a constrained Markov decision process that couples access coverage satisfaction with multi-hop transport feasibility, including hop-by-hop rate-budget degradation and a minimum parent-connectivity requirement for fault tolerance. To solve the resulting large discrete planning problem, we propose a graph-based actor-critic approach that uses a Graph Attention Network v2 (GATv2) encoder with Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), and we develop a multi-stage curriculum learning strategy that progressively increases constraint difficulty and scenario diversity for stable training and transferable policies. In a 60 GHz urban simulation over a 1000 m x 1000 m area with multiple donor layouts, the trained policy satisfies the minimum coverage requirement of 98% with fewer deployed IAB nodes than learning and heuristic baselines, and maintains higher coverage under progressive backhaul failures. The results demonstrate that curriculum-trained graph-based reinforcement learning can improve deployment efficiency and resilience while transferring across heterogeneous IAB donor topologies without retraining.
item.dc:creator: Jie Zhang, Haochen Sun, Mingzhang Zhou, Paul D. Mitchell, Hamed Ahmadi, Qiang Ni

item.title: Mobility-Aware Task Offloading in Mobile Edge Computing-Empowered Space-Air-Ground Integrated Internet-of-Things Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.14102v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mobile edge computing (MEC)-empowered spaceair-ground integrated Internet-of-Things (IoT) networks (SAGIINs) provide a promising solution for computation-intensive tasks generated by mobile IoT devices (IDs). However, task offloading in SAGIINs is challenging due to time-varying IDto-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) channels, intermittent LEO satellite service availability, and the coupling among UAV trajectory, communication, computation, and energy decisions. This paper investigates an energy-efficient task offloading and UAV trajectory planning problem in an MEC-empowered SAGIIN, where one UAV acts as both an aerial relay and an MEC server, and multiple LEO satellites provide supplementary computing resources. The UAV trajectory planning, task splitting, and computing resource allocation are jointly optimized to minimize the total system energy consumption under task completion, communication, computation, flight region, and satellite service window constraints. The resulting non-convex problem is decomposed into a UAV trajectory planning subproblem and a task splitting and computing resource allocation subproblem. To solve the former, a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-assisted large language model (LLM)-enhanced deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm, termed RLD, is proposed. The latter is shown to be convex and can be solved by using CVXPY for a given UAV trajectory. A weighted retrieval score is further designed to balance ID mobility-pattern similarity and historical UAV trajectory energy performance. Simulation results show that RLD completes all computational tasks in previously unseen test scenarios while consuming less total energy than the benchmark algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Minghao Sun, Jinghuai Xiong, Xiaoli Chu, Zitian Zhang

item.title: Criticality-Aware RAN Function Placement for Robust 6G Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.14121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The disaggregation of base stations into radio access network (RAN) functions introduces new vulnerabilities to mobile networks, as disruptions in cloud locations can interrupt multiple RAN functions and trigger cascading failures, leading to widespread outages. In this paper, we propose a criticality-aware RAN function placement solution to improve the robustness of disaggregated mobile networks against random failures and targeted attacks. Our solution optimizes the placement of centralized units (CUs) and distributed units (DUs) across cloud locations to reduce functional dependencies and limit the criticality of cloud locations, while preserving the cost benefits of RAN function centralization. We formulate the placement as an optimization model that jointly minimizes functional dependency and placement cost, subject to criticality constraints, as well as computing and transport requirements. We numerically evaluated our approach on a real-world mobile network topology across multiple disruption scenarios and demonstrated that our solution improves robustness, yielding up to 75% more operational radio units (RUs) after disruptions than existing approaches.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel M. Almeida, Joao F. Santos, Walid Saad, Nicola Marchetti, Kleber V. Cardoso

item.title: One Rater to Score Them All: Frozen Large Language Model Anchoring for Video Quality of Experience
item.description: arXiv:2611.12916v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quality of Experience results for video streaming cannot be compared across studies, because public databases share neither test material nor subjects. This work introduces a common reference rater: an open-weights large language models with a fixed rubric and greedy decoding that scores the delivery events of every session and supplies the shared items that score equating requires. The rater is used without training, and it reads only the playback event log of startup delay, stalls and quality switches, which most delivery databases retain even when they share nothing else. A monotonic curve then maps each study's native scale onto the common scale. On 3{,}552 sessions from four studies covering four rating scales, the rater attains a Spearman correlation of 0.809 on VL04 of the ITU-T P.1203 collection, exceeding P.1203 mode~0 on the same sessions, with a Krippendorff alpha of 0.974 over repeated scoring and 0.951 across three serving providers. Sessions from three further laboratories give correlations from 0.756 to 0.787. After calibration, the four studies are placed on a single 0 to 100 scale with a held-out error between 7.8 and 13.3 points, and a mean VMAF of 60 corresponds to positions 17 points apart in two of the studies.
item.dc:creator: Parsa Hassani Shariat Panahi, Amir H. Jalilvand, M. Hassan Najafi

item.title: An Improved $(1+2e)$-Approximation Algorithm for Metric Data Placement
item.description: arXiv:2611.13224v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the metric data placement problem with site-capacity constraints and fixed installation costs, aiming to minimize the total cost of placing data (resources) and accessing their nearest copies. We develop a deterministic polynomial-time approximation algorithm based on a natural linear programming relaxation of the problem. Starting from an optimal fractional solution, we construct multiscale metric-ball partitions independently for each resource and connect overlapping balls at consecutive levels to form a flow network. The resource layers are then coupled through shared site-capacity arcs, allowing us to obtain an integral placement by minimizing a surrogate cost over a single min-cost circulation. By optimizing the choice of ball radii, we establish an approximation factor of $1+2e\approx 6.44$. To our knowledge, this is the best approximation guarantee for the metric data placement problem since its introduction by Baev and Rajaraman in 2001.
item.dc:creator: S. Rasoul Etesami

item.title: 5G CATS: 5G-Based Cryptographic Authorization Against Trafficking of Semiconductor Devices
item.description: arXiv:2611.13437v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Enforcing export controls on AI accelerators requires verifying where a chip operates after deployment. Round-trip time measurements can bound a chip's distance from a trusted landmark, but any jitter in honest replies forces the verifier to loosen its timeout, giving an attacker slack to relay traffic over fiber from a restricted region. Prior approaches either cross the untrusted host stack or rely on noisy power-line channels that inflate this slack. We present 5G CATS, a location certification system that pairs a co-packaged 5G radio, cryptographic engine, and hardware interlock on the GPU package with 5G Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communication (URLLC) base stations. Terminating the radio link inside the package removes the host software, PCIe fabric, and baseboard management controller from the verification path. We map an authenticated challenge-response protocol onto 5G's slot structure, replace permanent key erasure with short-lived execution leases, and specify a cross-check of the chip's reported serving cell against the carrier's own attachment records. In ns-3 and 5G-LENA simulations of an unloaded cell, our URLLC-based radio profile narrows the 99.9th percentile round-trip spread to 2.60 ms, more than ten times narrower than default 5G. A tracer rejects every round of a fiber relay from 300 km, against 2,000 km for default 5G. Against a 3,000 km attacker, a tracer stays safe at up to 1,410 km from the chip, against at most 619 km for PowerCATS's published model, while default 5G is never safe.
item.dc:creator: Sreevikram Rajaraman, Derek Ladd, Nicholas Heinrich-Barna, Srinivas Shakkottai, Jeyavijayan Rajendran

item.title: Exploring Synchrony for Communication in Modular Neural Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.13759v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: One motivation for modular neural networks is to divide computation across components that learn distinct, reusable functions, which could then be recombined to support compositional generalisation. In practice, modular structure alone does not guarantee that such roles develop, and unrestricted communication between modules can undermine any specialisation that does emerge. This raises the question of how modular communication should be organised. The problem can be viewed as an analogue of the perceptual binding problem, where synchrony has been proposed as a mechanism for coordinating distributed representations. We introduce SyncNet, a modular architecture that separates module content from a dynamical phase state: learnt Kuramoto dynamics evolve the phases, while phase alignment determines communication through a shared channel. We evaluate SyncNet on Sort-of-CLEVR for relational reasoning and on SQOOP for systematic generalisation, where lower pair variety demands more recombination at test time. SyncNet gives the best held-out accuracy of the models compared at the three lowest pair varieties, by 5.1 percentage points at the hardest, and is competitive on Sort-of-CLEVR though below the strongest attention baselines. Test-time overrides show that performance depends on phases that evolve: fixed phases cost as much as no addressing at all, and permuting which module holds which region is nearly as damaging. A content-addressed variant trained from scratch nonetheless matches it, so the benefit appears to come from the modular decomposition rather than synchrony itself.
item.dc:creator: Nikolas Willems, Qiyang Sun, Bj\"{o}rn W. Schuller

item.title: Verifiable Agentic Traffic Class: A Policed Quality-of-Service Mechanism for Agentic AI Traffic, Evaluated from Simulation to Real-Kernel Adversarial Testing
item.description: arXiv:2611.14211v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Software agents built on large language models generate traffic unlike human web traffic, yet routers have no class for it and cannot verify a sender's claim to be an agent. This paper proposes the Verifiable Agentic Traffic Class (VATC), which combines a reserved Differentiated Services Code Point (DSCP) value declaring agent traffic, a router-side classifier that demotes flows contradicting the declaration to a class served after best-effort traffic, and a rate-limited priority queue. VATC was compared with static Differentiated Services (DiffServ), a dedicated class that trusts the marking, and fq_codel, a per-flow fair-queuing scheduler, in two simulators and on a real Linux kernel. VATC matched DiffServ under steady load. In a constructed burst it cut mean agent queuing delay by 98% relative to DiffServ in simulation (assuming an immediate verdict), at a 12% increase in human delay; most of the gain came from the separate class. Under a spoofed flood in the kernel, the rate limit held human latency 11 times below DiffServ's. Without verification, DiffServ and a tightly configured fq_codel gave legitimate agents lower latency than VATC; a live four-feature classifier then demoted all 20 bulk-shaped spoofers and gave agents 0.30 ms, but missed six spoofers that copied the agent pattern. With emulated network delay, a timing feature of the classifier stopped separating agent from human flows. In real agent harnesses on a congested link, router queueing took 13% to 63% of task time, depending on harness and assumed model latency. The traffic was synthetic or sandbox-scale.
item.dc:creator: Naveen Babu Narayanan Nair, Sajay Kurup

item.title: PSL-RGHA: Parallel Split Learning with Reference Gradient Half-Space Alignment for Mitigating Gradient Divergence
item.description: arXiv:2611.14312v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The escalating complexity of deep neural networks hinders the deployment of federated learning (FL) on resource-constrained devices, especially for multimedia applications such as on-device image classification and speech recognition. Parallel split learning (PSL) has emerged as a promising solution by offloading a substantial portion of the computational workload to the server through layer-wise model partitioning, making it particularly suitable for resource-limited visual and speech intelligence scenarios. However, the absence of client-side aggregation renders PSL sus ceptible to severe training divergence and potential convergence failure under heterogeneous data distributions. To address this challenge, we propose PSL-RGHA, a gradient-aligned PSL framework that employs reference gradient half-space alignment mechanism to mitigate training divergence among client devices. PSL-RGHA comprises two novel components: reference gradient progressive construction (RGPC) and gradient half-space alignment (GHA). Specifically, RGPC evaluates the directional consistency of client gradients and progressively synthesizes a robust reference gradient via Weiszfeld updates, effectively approximating the global descent direction. Then, GHA constrains client gradients within the reference half-space defined by RGPC to mitigate gradient conflicts and rectify local updates. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our PSL-RGHA framework outperforms existing baselines in various settings.
item.dc:creator: Han Li, Zheng Lin, Miao Yang, Zehang Lin, Jing Yang, Zihan Fang, Qiyang Zhang, Zhaolu Kang, Jianmin Li, Lin Li, Mingwei Hong, Shunzhi Zhu

item.title: fRAC: Remote Accelerator Calls on Hostless FPGAs
item.description: arXiv:2504.04404v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Hardware accelerators are essential for meeting microsecond-scale demands in distributed applications, but invoking them over the network remains bottlenecked by host software. Host-mediated paths (RPC, RDMA) still rely on the CPU to reassemble requests and launch accelerators, which dominates end-to-end latency, while packet-level offload on SmartNICs lacks any notion of a complete request. We introduce the Remote Accelerator Call (RAC) paradigm, in which transport ingestion, request reassembly, dispatch, and accelerator invocation are handled entirely in hardware. We build fRAC, a hostless prototype that implements this network-to-accelerator interface as a lightweight shim on an FPGA hosting multiple virtualized accelerators, reconfigurable at runtime in a few milliseconds. Serverless functions backed by fine-grained accelerators are a natural fit, since host-mediated invocation overhead can match or exceed their short execution times. fRAC achieves under 7.8us end-to-end latency while sustaining application throughput of up to 90 Gbps. Compared to highly optimized DPDK-based CPU and DPU baselines, it achieves at least 80% lower latency under saturation, while consuming 85% less power.
item.dc:creator: Ziyi Yang, Krishnan B. Iyer, Yixi Chen, Ran Shu, Zsolt Istv\'an, Marco Canini, Suhaib A. Fahmy

item.title: Programmable GPU-Accelerated dApps for Real-Time Edge Inference and ISAC on NVIDIA Aerial Testbed
item.description: arXiv:2512.06493v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The transition of cellular networks to (i) software-based systems on commodity hardware and (ii) platforms for services beyond connectivity introduces critical system-level challenges. As sensing emerges as a key feature toward 6G standardization, supporting Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) with limited bandwidth and piggybacking on communication signals, while maintaining high reliability and performance, remains a fundamental challenge. In this paper, we provide two key contributions. First, we present a programmable, open-source framework for processing PHY signals through real-time, GPU-accelerated Artificial Intelligence (AI) applications on the edge Radio Access Network (RAN) infrastructure. Building on the Open RAN dApp architecture, the framework interfaces with a GPU-accelerated gNB based on NVIDIA Aerial Testbed (ATB), feeding PHY data to custom AI logic with about 84 $\mu$s of framework latency per slot and control loops with inference in about 123 $\mu$s for lightweight TensorRT models, multiple inference engines, and support for several AI backends. We evaluate the framework on two GPU platforms, with different GPU sharing modes and an increasing number of cells and dApps. Second, we demonstrate the framework capabilities through cuSense, an indoor localization dApp that consumes uplink DMRS channel estimates, removes static multipath components, and runs a neural network to infer the position of a moving person. Evaluated on a 3GPP-compliant 5G NR deployment, cuSense achieves a mean localization error of 73 cm on runs unseen during training, with 79% of predictions falling within 1 meter, and runs live in 241 $\mu$s, without dedicated sensing hardware or modifications to the 5G signals. The framework is released as open source, together with the cuSense dataset, providing a reference design for future AI-native RANs and ISAC applications.
item.dc:creator: Davide Villa, Mauro Belgiovine, Nicholas Hedberg, Michele Polese, Chris Dick, Tommaso Melodia

item.title: SplitCom: Communication-efficient Split Federated Fine-tuning of LLMs via Temporal Compression
item.description: arXiv:2602.10564v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Federated fine-tuning of on-device large language models (LLMs) mitigates privacy concerns by preventing raw data sharing. However, the intensive computational and memory demands pose significant challenges for resource-constrained edge devices. To overcome these limitations, split federated learning (SFL) emerges as a promising solution that partitions the model into lightweight client-side and compute-intensive server-side sub-models, thus offloading the primary training workload to a powerful server. Nevertheless, the high-dimensional activation exchanges in SFL lead to excessive communication overhead. To overcome this, we propose SplitCom, a communication-efficient SFL framework for LLMs that exploits temporal redundancy in activations across consecutive training epochs. Inspired by video compression, the core innovation of our framework lies in selective activation uploading only when a noticeable deviation from previous epochs occurs. To balance communication efficiency and learning performance, we introduce two adaptive threshold control schemes based on 1) bang-bang control or 2) deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG)-based reinforcement learning. Moreover, we implement dimensionality reduction techniques to alleviate client-side memory requirements. Furthermore, we extend SplitCom to the U-shape architecture, ensuring the server never accesses clients' labels. Extensive simulations and laboratory experiments demonstrate that SplitCom reduces uplink communication costs by up to 98.8\,\% in its standard configuration and total communication costs by up to 95.8\,\% in its U-shape variant without noticeably compromising model performance.
item.dc:creator: Tao Li, Yulin Tang, Yiyang Song, Cong Wu, Xihui Liu, Pan Li, Xianhao Chen

item.title: Bridge: Optimizing Collective Communication Schedules in Reconfigurable Networks with Reusable Subrings
item.description: arXiv:2605.12766v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Optical circuit-switched networks have emerged as an appealing alternative to electrical fabrics as they can reconfigure the network topology at runtime, reducing communication cost and improving bandwidth utilization. Yet exploiting optical reconfigurable networks for collective communication comes with a fundamental trade-off: each reconfiguration incurs non-negligible delay and the benefit of a new topology depends on future traffic. The central question is therefore when reconfiguration is worth its cost. While prior work has demonstrated the benefits of reconfiguration, the opportunity to reuse optical links to optimize multiple steps remains largely unexplored. In this paper, we present Bridge, a reconfiguration strategy for frequently used collective communication primitives, namely All-to-All, AllReduce, Reduce-Scatter, and AllGather. Bridge exploits the structure of Bruck's communication pattern to support efficient sparse reconfiguration. The key idea is to reduce propagation and transmission delay by directly connecting immediate communication partners and preserve efficient reachability to future peers through connected subrings. As a result, optical links can be reused across multiple subsequent steps, allowing the benefit of reconfiguration to amortize beyond a single step. Our evaluation shows that Bridge reduces All-to-All completion time by typically 3x to 10x over static baselines and is effective even with millisecond-scale reconfiguration delays; for AllReduce up to 1.5x against existing reconfiguration strategies, and by 1.5x to 6.6x against the Ring algorithm on low to moderate-sized workloads.
item.dc:creator: Anton Juerss, Stefan Schmid

item.title: A Lightweight, Open-Source Network Digital Twin Blueprint for IoT-Edge Environments
item.description: arXiv:2606.24853v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: IoT-Edge-Cloud infrastructures are increasingly heterogeneous, and experimenting across the continuum is difficult and risks disrupting live systems. Network Digital Twins (NDT) are a pragmatic answer, yet practitioners lack a structured account of three things: how to build an NDT from open tools, how to model wireless impairments, and how to understand whether the twin is faithful to the physical network, or not. This tutorial introduces NDT through the IRTF reference model and walks through a lightweight open-source blueprint built on Containerlab, Open vSwitch, \textit{Open Network Operating System (ONOS)}, and Prometheus/Grafana. It then explains how to define wireless impairment profiles (static, model-based, trace-driven, AI-generated, and live), and what each approach can and cannot reproduce. Finally, it presents a workflow to validate the twin against the physical network. A proof-of-concept Edge case study illustrates the procedure, including the pitfalls encountered and the lessons learned. Directions for future research are outlined.
item.dc:creator: Josevany do Amaral, Rute C. Sofia

item.title: Distributed Hybrid Quantum-Classical Optimization for Robust AoII Minimization in Satellite-Ground Integrated Edge Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.05651v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Edge servers acting on monitored processes need estimates that are correct, not just recent. In satellite-ground integrated networks (SGINs), handover and shadowing interrupt links long enough for the process to change state several times, motivating the age of incorrect information (AoII). We formulate VANGUARD, a robust problem that jointly sets update rates, association, and bandwidth to minimize the worst-case AoII across disruption scenarios, and we solve it with SENTINEL, a distributed hybrid quantum-classical procedure. A renewal-interval decomposition yields a closed-form cost per delivery interval for AoII. The minimax is dualized into classically updated scenario weights, so each domain solves a linear assignment encoded as a compact quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem with XY-mixer-enforced one-hot constraints; domains are coordinated by the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), and every schedule is certified by its exact worst-case AoII. Under Starlink passes and the 3GPP TR 38.811 channel, the certificate held in 98.7\% of epochs, and the robust one was 2 to 7\% below the nominal one at no cost in realized AoII. The compact encoding uses four to six times fewer qubits than an epigraph encoding; thirteen domains, each 8 to 38 qubits, run on IBM Heron processors and are decoded to the exact optimum.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Arif Hossain, Tanzimul Alam Fahim, Weiqi Liu, Nirwan Ansari

item.title: Packet Interval Modulation for Uncoordinated NFC Data Networking Around Meander E-Textiles
item.description: arXiv:2610.35870v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Smart home sensing with low-power wireless nodes is non-intrusive but requires battery maintenance and cannot identify residents. A garment with a meander-coil NFC reader solves both, as it powers battery-free tags on the skin and on nearby objects and attributes every reading to its wearer. Because the number of tags in range changes as the user moves, we propose packet interval modulation (PIM), which encodes sensor values into pulse intervals without reader commands. With five tags, PIM reduces the collision rate of slotted ALOHA from 22.7% to 4.1% while delivering 384 bps, enabling resident-attributed ambient sensing.
item.dc:creator: Shigemi Ishida, Satoshi Ido, Ryo Takahashi

item.title: Holonic Graceful Transitions Across Centralized, Decentralized, Distributed, and Local Control in DER-rich Cyber-Power Distribution System
item.description: arXiv:2609.27759v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The increasing penetration of distributed energy resources (DERs) in distribution system necessitates adaptive coordination frameworks. These frameworks must remain optimal during normal operation and resilient under cyber physical disturbances. Existing coordinated control approaches are typically deployed as static architectures with limited ability to adapt when communication degrades, local instability emerges, and operating conditions become spatially heterogeneous. This work addresses the gap by proposing a DER service-independent edge autonomous holonic adaptive coordination framework. In this framework, each DER controller executes its own control actions and transitions among centralized, distributed, decentralized, and local autonomous coordination modes without always relying on static coordination commands from the grid operator. The framework preserves coordination continuity across modes by retaining local controller states while reconfiguring only the coordination topology, information exchange pattern, and fallback action associated with the active DER service. Graceful transitions are enabled through dwell timers, rate limiting, and safety overrides to prevent dynamic instability during mode changes. Volt VAR control is used as a representative distribution automation application to validate the proposed architecture in a cyber-physical Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testbed. The proposed approach is evaluated under diverse cyber-physical event-based scenarios, showing region-confined adaptation under localized disturbance, reduced coordination traffic during coordination switching, and node-confined mitigation under cyber attack through edge anomaly detection and neighbor-corroborated impact estimation.
item.dc:creator: Md Fazley Rafy, Niloy Patari, Anurag K. Srivastava
